description: The IChemE Accident Database is a legacy collection of more than 10,500 records of process industry accidents and incidents, developed in 1997 with the last entry made in 2000. It is published by the Institution of Chemical Engineers through its Safety Centre, which no longer sells the database but offers the data free as PDF files grouped by activity (operational, processing, transportation), cause (chemical, equipment, external, human, management system, process, utility failure and others), consequence (environmental, explosion, fire, implosion, near miss, people, plant and transport effects), equipment type, from piping and reactors to storage and power plant, and substance, in alphabetical ranges. Coverage is international process industry incidents. The PDFs are available free to download; the page read gives no licence. Caveats: IChemE does not warrant the accuracy of the data, will not verify or update it, and points users to more current databases, so it is a historical resource. For simulation it gives classified historical incidents, including utility failures, to estimate how often equipment types fail and which causes lead to fires or explosions in hazard and resilience studies of chemical plants. It is related to the IChemE lessons learned database record in this catalogue, a current curated set of incident summaries.
